learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.

observations.prediction: Selected water as containing more particles than carbon and locked it in. The question explicitly counts each atom or molecule as one particle.
observations.exploration: Pressed 12 g carbon: one mole, 6.02 times ten to power23 particles, box100%. Pressed 18 g water: identical count and fill, unlocking reveal. Set water mass9 g: half mole,3.01 times ten to power23,box50%.
observations.reveal: Corrected about the same. Refers to both full-box observations, explains heavier water molecules rather than more particles. Defines mole as count and molar mass as weight of that count; names iron56 g.
observations.visual: Inline full-water screenshot inspected: pink particle dots fill green-outlined box,18 g scale label,scientific-notation count and100% badge. Controls and units legible. Trust count6/6 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
